title: Compact burst shaping and heuristic kernel selector for embedding endpoint tail reduction
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Background: Production embedding endpoints are experiencing sporadic p99 spikes during short bursts of high QPS from certain customers. Existing measures (larger micro-batches and conservative kernel defaults) reduce average cost but increase tail latency under bursty ingress patterns. This ticket proposes two coordinated changes: (1) a compact burst-shaper at the ingress layer that fragments very short-lived bursts into controlled mini-windows to avoid straggler-induced kernel spin, and (2) a lightweight heuristic kernel selector that switches to low-latency kernels for small-window workloads. Together these aim to reduce embedding p99 by 25-40% for bursty tenants while keeping unit cost within 5% of baseline.

Goals (measurable):
- Reduce per-tenant embedding API p99 latency for bursty patterns by >= 25% on average across testbench traces.
- Keep median latency within +/-10% of today.
- Ensure per-token compute cost impact <= 5% for workloads in the benchmark suite.
- Safe rollout path with canary and gradual expand; automatic fallback to current scheduler on regressions.

Hypothesis & rationale:
- Burst spikes are short enough that packing into a single larger micro-batch causes tail amplification when a straggler enters the kernel execution window. Compacting bursts into deterministic mini-windows (50-200ms) reduces cross-request variance and allows the runtime to pick kernels tuned for short sequences.
- Many kernels offer a tradeoff: faster startup and lower latency for small sequence length vs higher throughput for large aggregated batches. A heuristic selector can pick the low-latency kernel when estimated batch size and sequence-length distribution indicate bursts.

Design overview:
1) Burst shaper (ingress):
   - New lightweight gate in the vector endpoint proxy that tracks burst pulses per tenant (sliding window QPS + burst factor). For bursts detected above threshold T1, instead of merging into current draining window we create a compact mini-window of duration D (configurable, default 100ms) with a tight max_item cap.
   - Mini-windows are allowed to be processed even if underutilized to avoid waiting for slow arrivals.
   - Expose config flags per-tenant (enable/disable, D, max_items) via tenant config in control plane.

2) Heuristic kernel selector (runtime):
   - Adds a fast admission check that uses the mini-window metadata (estimated batch size, avg sequence length, quantization profile) to pick between Kernel-A (latency-optimized) and Kernel-B (throughput-optimized).
   - Selector maintains an online success metric (latency delta and cost delta) and reverts to default kernel if sliding-window performance degrades.

Telemetry and metrics to capture:
- Per-tenant p50/p95/p99 latency before/after for synthetic burst traces and production sampling.
- Kernel pick ratio and per-kernel latency/cost breakdown.
- Mini-window creation frequency, avg fill-factor, and timeout occurrences.
- Tail-cases where fallback triggered and reason codes.

Experiment plan:
- Local prototype against the embedding testbench (historical traces from 10 tenants with bursty patterns). Measure p50/p95/p99 and per-token cost.
- Canary on staging cluster for one tenant group (noop by default; record-only for 48 hours). Validate telemetry.
- Gradual canary: enable for 5% traffic of selected tenants with real traffic shaping rules. Monitor alerting thresholds (p99, error rate, cost delta).
- Full rollout gated by automated A/B stats (p99 reduction, non-regression of median, cost delta <= 5%).

Acceptance criteria:
- In testbench, median p99 reduction >= 25% across selected bursts without >5% cost increase.
- No increase in error rates or retries in canary stage.
- Safe rollback works within 60s to prior scheduler.

Implementation milestones:
- Week 1: Ingress burst shaper prototype and control-plane flags (Ava)
- Week 2: Heuristic selector stub in runtime + unit tests (Ravi)
- Week 3: Integration test with simulated traces + telemetry dashboards (Ravi, SRE)
- Week 4: Staging canary (record-only) and iterate on thresholds (Ava)
- Week 5: Small production canary and rollout playbook (SRE/ops)

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Mis-detection of bursts may degrade throughput for steady high QPS tenants. Mitigation: conservative default thresholds, per-tenant opt-out, and offline tuning using tenant traces.
- Risk: Kernel selector oscillates between kernels on noisy signals. Mitigation: add hysteresis and minimum dwell time before switching.
- Risk: Increased memory pressure due to parallel mini-windows. Mitigation: enforce global per-host mini-window caps and backpressure to ingress.

- Design notes: https://redwood.atlassian.com/confluence/embedding-burst-shaper (internal)
- Prototype branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2741 (WIP)
- Telemetry dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.company/d/embeddings/burst-shaper-canary

Next steps:
- Finalize mini-window sizing heuristics after 1 week of staging telemetry.
- Add a small synthetic harness that can replay production traces into staging for night-long stress tests.
- Prepare rollout playbook with rollback criteria and oncall contacts.
